rules.title: Three-day Notice to Quit for disorderly, destructive or rule-violating conduct
rules.requirement: A three-day written Notice to Quit is required before eviction for causes described as disorderly, destructive or violating written rules or lease provisions. No further notice is required before suing to evict a tenant who stays after failing to pay rent.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants evicted for disorderly, destructive or rule/lease-violating conduct
rules.quoted_span: A three-day written Notice to Quit is required for any of the causes described as disorderly, destructive or violative of written rules or lease provisions (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2(a)).

rules.title: Non-renewal eviction in owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings
rules.requirement: A tenant in an owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling may be evicted after the lease expires if the landlord has given written notice for delivery of possession. A three-month notice to quit is required for an at will or year-to-year tenancy and a one-month notice for a month-to-month tenancy.
rules.key_value: three-month notice (at will or year-to-year); one-month notice (month-to-month)
rules.coverage_text: Tenants residing in owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings
rules.citation: New Jersey Truth in Renting guide (no statute cited for this rule)
rules.quoted_span: In addition to the causes listed above, a tenant residing in an owner- occupied two- or three-family dwelling may be evicted if the landlord can show that the tenant is staying after the expiration of the lease and the landlord has given the tenant a written notice for delivery of possession of the property.

rules.title: Rooming and boarding house evictions
rules.requirement: Owners of rooming and boarding houses must follow the good causes and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, unless otherwise ordered by the Bureau, and must give at least three (3) working days' notice to the County Welfare Board before starting an eviction action for any resident.
rules.key_value: at least three (3) working days' notice to the County Welfare Board
rules.coverage_text: Rooming and boarding houses: buildings with at least two (2) living units occupied by unrelated persons without private kitchens and bathrooms, unless an exception in the Rooming and Boarding House Act applies
rules.exemptions: Hotels with more than 85 percent temporary occupancy by people with homes elsewhere, school and college dormitories, buildings housing only college students and certain residences for the disabled; or if otherwise ordered by the Bureau
rules.quoted_span: The Regulations Governing Rooming and Boarding Houses, which are enforced by the Bureau of Rooming and Boarding House Standards of the Department of Community Affairs, require owners of rooming and boarding houses to follow the good causes and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, except if otherwise ordered by the Bureau (N.J.A.C. 5:27-3.3(c)).

rules.title: Public housing evictions
rules.requirement: Public housing authorities must follow State eviction laws and HUD regulations; a public housing tenant may request a hearing after receiving a notice of termination, and the authority may not begin a court eviction until the hearing decision has been mailed or delivered and a notice to vacate served.
rules.quoted_span: In the case of an eviction, a public housing tenant may request a hearing from the housing authority after receiving a notice of termination of tenancy.

rules.title: Owner personal occupancy requirement after eviction
rules.requirement: When a tenant vacates after notice that the landlord wishes to personally occupy the unit, the landlord must occupy the unit for at least six (6) months.
rules.coverage_text: Units vacated after a notice that the landlord wishes to personally occupy the unit
rules.penalty: If the landlord instead permits occupancy by another tenant or registers conversion to a condominium or cooperative, the landlord is liable to the former tenant for three (3) times the damages suffered plus attorney fees and costs.
rules.quoted_span: When a tenant vacates a dwelling unit after having been given notice that the  landlord wishes to personally occupy the unit the landlord must occupy the unit for at least six (6) months.

rules.title: No residential use after eviction for board-up, demolition or removal from residential use
rules.requirement: When a tenant vacates after notice that the landlord seeks to permanently board up, demolish or retire the building from residential use, the landlord must not use the property for residential use for five (5) years.
rules.coverage_text: Properties where tenants vacated after notice of permanent board-up, demolition or retirement from residential use
rules.penalty: Landlord or former landlord may be liable to the tenant for three (3) times the damages plus attorney fees and costs, and a civil penalty up to $10,000.00 for each violation; the property may not be registered as a planned real estate development during the five-year period.
rules.quoted_span: When a tenant vacates a dwelling unit after having been given notice that the landlord seeks to permanently board up or demolish the building or to permanently retire it from residential use, the landlord must not use this property for residential use for a period of five (5) years.

rules.title: Reprisal - Civil Rights of Tenants
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot retaliate by eviction, substantial alteration of a lease or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises protected rights, such as enforcing lease or legal rights, making good faith complaints to government authorities, or joining a tenant organization.
rules.coverage_text: All rental properties used for dwelling purposes, including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings
rules.penalty: The tenant may sue the landlord for damages in a civil action.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-10.10).  The law against reprisal applies to all rental properties used for dwelling purposes, including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.

rules.title: Foreclosure not grounds for eviction; 90-day notice to quit
rules.requirement: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction; a tenant may be evicted due to foreclosure only after a 90-day notice to quit when the buyer wants to personally occupy the property as a primary residence, and not before the tenant's lease expires.
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenants in foreclosed properties, including month-to-month tenants and two- and three-family owner-occupied units
rules.citation: Chase Manhattan Bank v. Josephson, 135 N.J. 209 (1994)
rules.quoted_span: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction in New Jersey.
rules.interaction_text: However, the federal law does not preempt any State or local law that provides longer time periods or other additional protections for tenants  in foreclosure proceedings .

rules.title: Notice to tenants after foreclosure sale
rules.requirement: Any person acquiring a foreclosed property with residential rental units must notify tenants in English and Spanish within 10 business days after the sale that ownership has changed and that they are not required to move because of the foreclosure.
rules.key_value: within 10 business days after the sale
rules.coverage_text: Foreclosed properties containing one or more residential rental units
rules.quoted_span: Any person acquiring a foreclosed property containing one or more residential rental units must provide notices to the tenants in English and Spanish, within 10 business days after the sale, letting tenants know that ownership has changed hands and that the tenants are not required to move because of the foreclosure.

rules.title: Foreclosure Fairness Act - voluntary bona fide offers to vacate
rules.requirement: A foreclosing party or new landlord may make a written bona fide monetary offer for the tenant to vacate, but acceptance is voluntary and the tenant may not be pressured to accept; prohibited pressure tactics include misrepresenting rights, harassment and excessive rent increases.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants in foreclosed properties receiving offers to vacate
rules.quoted_span: The tenant shall not be pressured by anyone, including the person making the offer to accept any offer to vacate the property.

rules.title: Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act
rules.requirement: Eligible senior citizen, disabled or qualifying veteran tenants in buildings being converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership may be protected from eviction for 40 years if their family income is not more than three (3) times the average per person income in their county or $50,000.00, whichever is greater.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants at least 62 years old before the conversion recording date, permanently disabled, or qualifying disabled veterans, who have lived in a building being converted for at least one (1) year before the conversion recording date
rules.quoted_span: Tenants may be protected from eviction for 40 years if their family income is not more than three (3) times the average per person income in their county or $50,000.00, whichever  is greater (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.28).
